He played [[college basketball]] for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]]. He was drafted with the 20th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=Tony Snell Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |url=http://www.nba.com:80/playerfile/tony_snell/bio/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160301073725/http://www.nba.com:80/playerfile/tony_snell/bio/ |archive-date=2016-03-01 |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} He is also the first NBA player to be state publicly that he had been [[diagnosed]] with [[autism]].{{Cite web |title= Former NBA player Tony Snell diagnosed with autism at age 31, says it made his life 'make so much sense'|date=June 16, 2023 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/former-nba-player-tony-snell-diagnosed-with-autism-at-age-31-says-it-made-his-life-make-so-much-sense/}} Born in the [[Watts, Los Angeles|Watts]] neighborhood of [[Los Angeles]], California, Snell was raised primarily by his mother, Sherika Brown, who worked multiple jobs as a single parent.{{cite news |last=Nickel |first=Lori |title=Basketball, family one and the same to Bucks' Tony Snell |newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |date=January 12, 2018 |url=https://eu.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2018/01/12/basketball-family-one-same-bucks-tony-snell/1015032001/}} Snell moved to [[Phoenix, Arizona]], before his senior year to finish high school at [[Westwind Preparatory Academy]]. He was the starting shooting guard for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]] in his sophomore and junior seasons, helping lead the Lobos to back-to-back [[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC) regular-season and conference tournament championships as well as [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] bids. ==High school career== Snell attended [[Martin Luther King High School (Riverside, California)|Martin Luther King High School]] in [[Riverside, California]], in 2008–09, where he and teammate [[Kawhi Leonard]],{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=3964877 |title=Leonard's stock keeps rising |last=Francisco |work=ESPN.com|date=March 9, 2009 |first=Joel}} a future two-time [[NBA Finals MVP]],{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=K.C. |title=Bulls rookie Snell a Pippen clone? |newspaper=Chicago Tribune |date=July 15, 2013 |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/07/15/bulls-rookie-snell-a-pippen-clone/}} : Snell has said that he remained in contact with former high school teammate Kawhi Leonard during his early NBA years, seeking advice as he adjusted to the league. led the Wolves to a 30–3 season and a number 7 national ranking in the [[MaxPreps]]/National Guard computer rankings.{{cite web |url=http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209088320 |title=Tony Snell Bio |publisher=New Mexico Athletics Official Site |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141214174910/http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209088320 |archive-date=December 14, 2014 }} In 2015, Leonard publicly expressed pride in Snell's development when the two faced each other in the NBA.{{cite news |last=McDonald |first=Jeff |title=An NBA reunion awaits Leonard, Snell |newspaper=San Antonio Express-News |date=March 7, 2015 |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/An-NBA-reunion-awaits-Leonard-Snell-6121409.php}} Snell averaged 14 points, seven rebounds, four blocks and five assists per game. In 2009 Snell enrolled at [[Westwind Preparatory Academy]] in Phoenix, where he averaged 19.5 points, 10 rebounds, 8.8 assists, 2.7 steals and 1.8 blocks.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/CnJRR-hTFkmLV7g6Z-4ppw/basketball-winter-09-10/profile-tony-snell.htm |title=Tony Snell Basketball Profile - Westwind Prep International 09-10 - MaxPreps |publisher=MaxPreps.com}} At Westwind he was a teammate of [[Jamaal Franklin]], who went on to play for [[San Diego State University]] and was drafted by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2013. ==College career== ===2010–11 season: Freshman year=== {{main|2010–11 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team}} In 2009, ESPN scouting reports called Snell "one of the top sleepers on the West Coast" and a "diamond in the rough".{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/evaluation?id=79273 |title=Basketball Recruiting - Tony Snell - Player Profiles |work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 12, 2026}} Snell committed to play for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]] on September 15, 2009, and signed in November 2009.{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/newmexico/basketball/recruiting/player-Tony-Snell-103826 |title=Tony Snell |publisher=Rivals.com}} The 2010–11 Lobo squad was young and inexperienced, led by lone senior [[Dairese Gary]] and UCLA transfer [[Drew Gordon]].Stevens, Richard. [http://www.golobos.com/fls/26000/pdf/mbasketball/weekly-release10-11.pdf Lobo Basketball Game Notes 2010-11] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140401081445/http://www.golobos.com/fls/26000/pdf/mbasketball/weekly-release10-11.pdf |date=April 1, 2014 }}, Season Recap, p.2. Snell was one of four freshmen playing significant minutes, along with [[Kendall Williams]], [[Alex Kirk]] and [[Cameron Bairstow]], one of the most accomplished recruiting classes in Lobo history.[http://www.abqjournal.com/363401/sports/this-lobo-class-was-one-of-classiest-ever.html ''This Lobo class was one of classiest ever''], Albuquerque Journal, March 6, 2014. The team had a roller-coaster season, starting 10–1 and later winning four straight twice, but also losing four straight and six of nine. They beat number 3 [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in Provo late in the season, but lost to the Cougars in the MWC tournament. The Lobos received a bid to the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament]] and beat UTEP before losing at Alabama to finish the season 22–13. Snell played in all but one game, averaging 4.4 points and two rebounds.Lobo Game Notes 2010-11, p.54 He scored in double-figures four times and led the team in scoring twice. He had a breakout performance with 16 points against then-number 9 BYU, hitting four three-pointers, followed two games later by a season-best 19, with five threes, against [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]]. He started seven games, averaging 8.3 points in his starts, and in one seven-game stretch he averaged 10.3 points a game and shot 17 of 31 (.548) from three. A sprained ankle late in the season limited his play and cut his production, as he managed just 11 points in the last eight games of the season. ===2011–12 season: Sophomore year=== {{main|2011–12 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team}} The Lobos in 2011–12 were anchored by the dominant inside play of Gordon, who tallied 19 [[double-double]]s and whose 11.1 rebounds per game were fourth in the nation.Stevens, Richard. [http://www.themw.com/#!/news-detail/sports-m-baskbl-spec-rel-041012aad ''New Mexico Lobo Men's Basketball 2011-12 Season Review''], MWC Official Site, April 10, 2012. The team allowed just 59.3 points per game, the lowest ever for the Lobos in the shot clock era, and they held opponents under 40% shooting for the first time since the 1964–65 season. Their scoring defense was fourteenth nationally, and their defensive field goal percentage was seventh. Snell was among several young guards battling for playing time going into the season, as senior and three-year starter [[Phillip McDonald]] was hampered by injury.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/sports/2011/11/01/lobos-to-exhibit-talent.html |title=Lobos To Exhibit Talent |last=Smith |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=November 1, 2011|first=Mark}} Snell earned a starting spot after "tearing it up in practice" and playing well in preseason exhibition games.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/sports/2011/11/11/privateers-a-mystery-to-lobos.html |title=Privateers A Mystery To Lobos |last=Smith |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=November 11, 2011|first=Mark}} He was capable of explosive scoring, but he was also prone to becoming tentative and falling into slumps.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/sports/2012/02/18/lobo-shell-comes-out-of-that-shell.html |title=Lobo Snell Comes Out of that Shell |last=Wright |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=February 18, 2012|first=Rick}} He scored in double-figures in twenty games, including three games over 20, twice scoring 24, hitting six threes in one of those games; yet he also scored six or fewer points in eleven games, going scoreless for two straight games at one point.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/sports/2012/02/17/the-national-stage-is-set.html |title=The National Stage Is Set |last=Smith |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=February 17, 2012|first=Mark}} For the season, Snell averaged 10.5 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.3 assists a game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/snellto01.html Tony Snell], Basketball-Reference.com The Lobos won thirteen straight early in the season on the way to a 15–2 record.Lobo Media Guide 2013-14, p.141. They lost their next two games to No. 16 San Diego State and at No. 14 UNLV but then won seven straight, avenging those losses and climbing into the top twenty with a 22–4 record. After two upset losses they settled for a share of the MWC regular-season championship. In the conference tournament semi-finals, the Lobos won at No. 20 UNLV, with Snell accounting for 15 points, six rebounds and six assists.New Mexico vs. UNLV, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=320690167 Boxscore], ESPN.com, March 9, 2012. The Lobos won the championship game over number 18 San Diego State, as Snell scored 14, shooting 4-6 from three, and was named to the All-Tournament team.New Mexico vs. San Diego State, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=320700021 Boxscore], ESPN.com, March 10, 2012.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/sports/2012/03/10/breaking-lobos-win-mountain-west-title.html |title=Lobos Are Best in the (Mountain) West |last=Smith |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=March 10, 2012|first=Mark}} New Mexico received a five-seed in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]], but Snell was a non-factor, shooting a combined 1-9 (1-8 from three) and scoring just three points as the Lobos beat Long Beach StateNew Mexico vs. Long Beach State, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=320750167 Boxscore], ESPN.com, March 15, 2012. then lost to Final Four-bound Louisville.New Mexico vs. Louisville, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=320770097 Boxscore], ESPN.com, March 17, 2012. The Lobos finished the season 28–7, and Snell was named Honorable Mention All-Mountain West.{{cite web|url=http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030512aad.html |title=Mountain West Announces 2011-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards |publisher=The Mountain West |date=March 5, 2012}} ===2012–13 season: Junior year=== {{main|2012–13 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team}} The 2012–13 Lobos again relied on tough defense and a balanced scoring attack, often coming from behind to grind out close wins. The team held opponents to sixty points a game and again held them under 40% shooting, while going 10–2 in games decided by six or fewer points.Lobo Media Guide 2013-14, pp.103,109,141. While Williams led the team at just 13.3 points a game, four players averaged in double-figures, and seven Lobo players led the team in scoring in individual games.Stevens, Richard. 2012-13 Season Review, Lobo Media Guide 2013-14, p.49. Snell led the team in ten games, including five straight during a late stretch when he averaged 19.8 a game and shot 22 of 39 (.564) from three-point range.[http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/nm/sports/w-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/release/release_20130120aaa.pdf Lobo Basketball Game Notes 2012-13] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728063721/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/nm/sports/w-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/release/release_20130120aaa.pdf |date=July 28, 2014 }}, p.57. On the season, Snell averaged 12.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.9 assists a game, and he led the team in three-point shooting percentage and, for the second straight season, free throw percentage.Lobo Media Guide 2013-14, pp.72,75. Over his career, he was the fifth most accurate free throw shooter in Lobo history. The Lobos began the season 12–0, including a win over number 19 Connecticut, and climbed to No. 16 in the polls. They lost a couple of games to eventual NCAA tournament teams South Dakota State and St. Louis, but also won at No. 8 Cincinnati. After a bad loss at No. 20 San Diego State, they won nine out of ten and clinched the MWC regular-season title, while reaching No. 11. Snell assumed more of a leadership role, an adjustment due to his quiet demeanor—his mother termed him the "silent assassin", a nickname that Lobo fans embraced.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/237968/sports/college/finding-2.html |title=Finding His Voice |last=Grammer |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=October 12, 2012|first=Geoff}} He scored 20 points or more in six games, 25 or more in three games, but he continued to struggle at times, scoring under ten points in 13 games, with a low of five. In the MWC tournament, Snell averaged 17.7 points a game while shooting 12 of 20 (.600) from three-point range. In the semi-final game against San Diego State, he made three three-pointers in 55 seconds as the Lobos built a large lead. In the championship game at UNLV, he shot 8 of 11 from the field, 5 of 7 from three, at one point scoring 13 straight points for the Lobos as they pulled away to seal their second straight tourney title.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/239186/sports/college/no-15-unm-repeats-as-mwc-tourney-champs.html |title=No. 15 UNM repeats as MWC tourney champs |last=Grammer |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=March 16, 2013|first=Geoff}} Snell was named tournament MVP and ESPN national player of the week for his performance.Lobo Game Notes 2012-13, pp.13-14. After the season, he was named Third Team All-MWC. New Mexico entered the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]] ranked No. 10 and received a three-seed. They suffered a disappointing upset to Harvard, however, to finish the season 29–6. The Lobos shot poorly, with Snell going 4 of 12, 1 of 6 from three, for just nine points.New Mexico vs. Harvard, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=330800167 Boxscore], ESPN.com, March 21, 2013. Snell chose to forgo his senior season and declared for the NBA draft. While his college numbers were not spectacular, NBA scouts noted that the Lobos' balanced offense limited his output, and they were impressed by his length, outside shooting, and greatly improved defense.{{citation |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/36835/sports/college/snell-to-test-his-stock-in-nba-draft.html |title=Snell to test his stock in NBA draft |last=Grammer |publisher=Albuquerque Journal |date=March 27, 2013|first=Geoff}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2013–2016)=== [[File:Tony Snell 11-Jan-14.jpg|thumb|right|Snell during his rookie season with the Bulls in 2014]] Snell was selected with the 20th overall pick in [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. On July 10, 2013, he signed with the Bulls[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-tony-snell-and-erik-murphy.html Bulls sign Tony Snell and Erik Murphy] and joined them for [[2013 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 11.8 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.99 steals in five games.[http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2013/players/sl_tony_snell/ 2013 Summer League Statistics] As a rookie in 2013–14, Snell appeared in 77 games for the Bulls, averaging 4.5 points and 1.6 rebounds per game. In July 2014, Snell re-joined the Bulls for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 20.0 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.8 assists in five games, earning All-NBA Summer League first team honors.[http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_tony_snell/ 2014 Summer League Statistics][http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/20/all-summer-league-teams/index.html Rice, Jr. named MVP, leads All-NBA Summer League team] He was reunited with former Lobo teammates Bairstow (2014 Bulls' draftee) and Williams on the Bulls' summer league squad.{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/428613/sports/exlobos-enjoy-being-reunited-in-summer-league.html |title=Ex-Lobos enjoy being together again |work=abqjournal.com |date=July 13, 2014 |access-date=July 13, 2014}} On February 10, 2015, he scored a career-high 24 points in the Bulls' 104–86 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].[https://www.nba.com/games/20150210/SACCHI/gameinfo.html Snell scores career-high 24 as Bulls rout Kings, 104-86] Snell became the Bulls' starting small forward to begin the 2015–16 season. Over the first 25 games of the season, Snell started in all but four. However, on December 21, he was removed from the team's regular rotation and over the next three games, he was credited with a "DNP" in two of the three.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/snellto01/gamelog/2016/ Tony Snell 2015-16 Game Log] With teammate [[Doug McDermott]] out injured on December 28 against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Snell got his chance to re-establish himself in the rotation, coming off the bench to score an equal team-high 22 points on 8-of-14 shooting in 27 minutes of action, helping the Bulls defeat the Raptors 104–97.[https://www.nba.com/games/20151228/TORCHI/gameinfo.html Snell, Gasol spark Bulls to 104-97 win over the Raptors] ===Milwaukee Bucks (2016–2019)=== On October 17, 2016, Snell was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Michael Carter-Williams]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-acquire-tony-snell-bulls|title=Bucks Acquire Tony Snell from the Bulls|work=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2026}} Entering the 2016-17 season, Snell was named as the starting shooting guard due to an injury suffered by [[Khris Middleton]]. After missing the Bucks' season-opener with a sprained left ankle,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899481|title=Henson's tip-in at buzzer leads Bucks past Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}} Snell made his debut for the team in their second game of the season on October 29, 2016, scoring six points in 21 minutes as a starter in a 110–108 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899481|title=Nets vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}} On December 26, 2016, he made a career-high six three-pointers and set a season high with 20 points in a 107–102 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899903|title=Porter, Wall push Wizards to 107-102 comeback win vs Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=December 27, 2016}} On February 24, 2017, in 28 minutes of play against the Utah Jazz, Snell recorded zero counting stats, falling just 22 seconds short of [[Joel Anthony]]'s record for most playing time in a game without recording a point, rebound, assist, steal or block.{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Andrew |date=2017-02-25 |title=Bucks' Tony Snell came within 22 seconds of a ridiculous NBA record |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/bucks-tony-snell-came-within-22-seconds-of-a-ridiculous-nba-record |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=foxsports.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportscasting.com/the-infamous-game-tony-snell-played-28-minutes-and-didnt-record-a-single-stat/|title = The Infamous Game Tony Snell Played 28 Minutes and Didn't Record a Single Stat|date = May 7, 2020}} On March 6, 2017, he had 18 of his season-high 21 in the first half of the Bucks' 112–98 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900329|title=Antetokounmpo, Snell lead Bucks past 76ers, 112-98|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} He surpassed that mark on March 28 with a career-high 26 points in a 118–108 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900498|title=Snell scores 26 points, Bucks beat Hornets 118-108|work=ESPN.com|date=March 28, 2017|access-date=March 28, 2017}} On April 22, 2017, he set playoff career highs with 19 points and five 3-pointers in an 87–76 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in Game 4 of their first-round playoff series; the loss tied the series at 2–2.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950413|title=Raptors beat Bucks 87-76 in slugfest, tie series at 2-2|work=ESPN.com|date=April 22, 2017|access-date=April 23, 2017}} With Milwaukee, Snell earned praise from head coach [[Jason Kidd]] for his steady two-way play and team-first approach, with Kidd highlighting his defense, shooting and fit within the team's culture.{{cite news |last=Gardner |first=Charles F. |title=Bucks' Tony Snell fills the bill with steady play |newspaper=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |date=March 15, 2017 |url=https://eu.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2017/03/15/bucks-tony-snell-fills-bill-steady-play/99186454/}} On July 31, 2017, Snell re-signed with the Bucks to a four-year, $44 million contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-tony-snell|title=Milwaukee Bucks Re-sign Tony Snell|work=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2026}}{{cite web|last=Velazquez|first=Matt|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2017/07/31/tony-snell-officially-signs-new-deal-bucks/524640001/|title=Tony Snell officially signs new four-year, $44 million deal with Bucks|work=jsonline.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=July 31, 2017}} The deal reportedly includes a player option after the third year and reachable incentives that would push his total earnings to $46 million. On March 23, 2018, he matched his season high with 18 points in a 118–105 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975829|title=Bucks overcome sluggish start to beat Bulls 118-105|work=ESPN.com|date=March 23, 2018|access-date=March 24, 2018}} ===Detroit Pistons (2019–2020)=== On June 20, 2019, Snell was traded, along with the draft rights to [[Kevin Porter Jr.]], to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Jon Leuer]].{{cite web |date=June 20, 2019 |title=Bucks Acquire Jon Leuer From Detroit |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-aquire-jon-leuer-detroit |access-date=June 20, 2019 |work=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last=Langlois |first=Keith |date=June 21, 2019 |title=Pistons jump start off-season by trading for Snell, pocketing extra picks |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/pistons-jump-start-season-trading-snell-pocketing-extra-picks |access-date=June 21, 2019 |work=NBA.com}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2021)=== On November 20, 2020, Snell and [[Khyri Thomas]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Dewayne Dedmon]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-acquire-tony-snell-detroit-pistons|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Tony Snell from Detroit Pistons|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2020|last=Finberg|first=Annie}} On March 11, 2021, Snell made a game-winning three-pointer at the buzzer to give the Hawks a 121–120 victory over the [[Toronto Raptors]], capping off a 15-point fourth-quarter comeback.{{cite web |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Watch Tony Snell drain game-winning three, Hawks beat Raptors |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/03/11/watch-tony-snell-drain-game-winning-three-hawks-beat-raptors/ |website=NBC Sports |access-date=May 26, 2021 |date=March 11, 2021}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022)=== On August 10, 2021, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] announced that they had signed Snell.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers sign Tony Snell|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-tony-snell|date=August 10, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 10, 2021}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2022)=== On February 8, 2022, Portland traded Snell, [[Larry Nance Jr.]] and [[CJ McCollum]] to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Josh Hart]], [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]], [[Tomáš Satoranský]], [[Didi Louzada]], a protected 2022 first-round draft pick, the better of New Orleans' and Portland's 2026 second-round draft picks and New Orleans' 2027 second-round draft pick.{{Cite press release|date=February 8, 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=TRAIL BLAZERS COMPLETE TRADE WITH NEW ORLEANS|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers}} ===Maine Celtics (2023–2024)=== On January 27, 2023, Snell was acquired by the [[Maine Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 27, 2023|access-date=January 27, 2023}} On August 8, 2023, the [[Golden State Warriors]] held a free agent workout with Snell.{{cite tweet|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=The Warriors are holding free-agent workouts with veterans Dion Waiters, Tony Snell, Kent Bazemore, Juan Toscano-Anderson, Harry Giles and Trey Burke at facility over next two weeks, sources tell me and @anthonyVslater. GS has multiple round of workouts to identify signings.|number=1689068243040755712|user=ShamsCharania|date=August 8, 2023|access-date=August 8, 2023|author-link=Shams Charania}} On October 29, he returned to Maine.{{cite web|title=Maine Celtics Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-102823|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=January 14, 2024}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2024–2025)=== On October 2, 2024, Snell was traded to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce Acquires Tony Snell|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-tony-snell|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 3, 2024}} ===Boulazac Basket Dordogne (2025–2026)=== On August 23, 2025, Snell signed with [[Boulazac Basket Dordogne]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.boulazac-basket-dordogne.com/tony-snell-648-matchs-de-nba-au-bbd/|title=Tony Snell, 648 Matchs De Nba Au BBD|last=|first=|date=August 23, 2025|website=boulazac-basket-dordogne.com|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=September 8, 2025}} In his second season game with Boulazac, on October 3, 2025, he scored 27 points against [[Cholet Basket]].{{cite web |last=Hippocrate |first=Julien |title=Betclic Élite. Cholet Basket a fini par user Boulazac |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/basket/cholet/direct-cholet-basket-accueille-boulazac-pour-confirmer-son-bon-depart-en-betclic-elite-6a75c9c3-c68f-4a4a-9dc1-c30acbedcf62 |website=Ouest-France |date=October 3, 2025 |access-date=October 4, 2025 |language=fr}} On February 1, 2026, Snell helped Boulazac earn a landmark road win at reigning French champion [[Paris Basketball]], as the club built a commanding lead in Paris with Snell among the key three-point contributors.{{cite news |last=Dages |first=Lionel |title=Basket-ball, Élite : un exploit majuscule pour Boulazac à Paris ! |newspaper=Dordogne Libre |date=February 1, 2026 |url=https://www.dordognelibre.fr/sport/basket/bbd/basket-ball-elite-un-exploit-majuscule-pour-boulazac-a-paris-27669783.php |language=fr}} During the first part of the 2025–26 season, Snell established himself as one of the most efficient three-point shooters in Betclic Élite, ranking fourth in the league with a 50.9% three-point percentage after 16 games played.{{cite news |last=Dubourg |first=Rafael |title=Tony Snell, la gâchette boulazacoise |newspaper=Sud Ouest |date=January 24, 2026 |language=fr}}{{cite web |title=Adresse à 3 points – Betclic Élite |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/MQR_PROA.html |website=L'Équipe |access-date=October 4, 2025 |language=fr }} His long-range shooting was publicly praised by his head coach, who highlighted both his remarkable accuracy from beyond the arc and his overall impact on the team.{{cite web |title=Esprit Sport – (4/5) Au plus près du Boulazac Basket Dordogne : Alexandre Ménard, coach : "la ferveur populaire transcende l'équipe" |url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/franceinter/podcasts/esprit-sport/esprit-sport-du-jeudi-04-decembre-2025-3255556 |website=France Inter |access-date=December 4, 2025 |last=Nour-Eddine Zidane |language=fr}} ===Cholet Basket (2026–present)=== On June 18, 2026, Snell signed with [[Cholet Basket]] of [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite Instagram |user=cholet_basket |postid=DZu9VwLGg2c |title=Nouvelle recrue |date=June 18, 2026}} ==Personal life== Snell met his wife, Ashley, at a barbecue hosted by his [[Chicago Bulls]] teammate [[Jimmy Butler]].{{cite web |last1=Fischer |first1=Jake |title=Tony Snell's mission to return to NBA is bigger than just basketball |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/tony-snells-mission-to-return-to-nba-is-bigger-than-just-basketball-142355012.html?fr=sycsrp_catchall |website=Yahoo! |access-date=February 2, 2024 |date=February 1, 2024}} They have two sons who were both diagnosed with [[autism]] spectrum disorder. On ''[[Today (American TV program)|The Today Show]]'' on June 16, 2023, Snell revealed that he was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder,{{Cite web |last=Chiari |first=Mike |title=NBA Veteran Tony Snell Says He Was Diagnosed with Autism at Age 31 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10079551-nba-veteran-tony-snell-says-he-was-diagnosed-with-autism-at-age-31 |access-date=2023-06-16 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} after the evaluation of his eldest son helped to realize similarities with his own experience. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA===
